title: Are you a bigger fan of Yorgos Lanthimos with or without Efthimis Filippou?

commenti.body: I think the Filippou colabs are vastly better. The Favourite and Poor Things are great, but they're nowhere near as thought-provoking, funny or as disturbing as the earlier films. Poor Things goes overboard with its style, essentially launching a maximalist firework at your face. Meanwhile, The Lobster, KoaSD and Dogtooth were able to get much more visceral reactions out of me without needing to much at all.

I haven’t seen Poor Things yet but your Yorgos ranking has me excited! Trying to go in as blind as possible (all I know is it’s a Frankenstein story and it’s sexually charged) but can’t wait to see it!

Poor Things is very funny. Maybe me putting it at #1 is recency bias and I can see myself putting it below Dogtooth and The Lobster eventually.

But they are hard to compare because they're very different. Also, I don't mind the fireworks.

Also I didn't find Killing of a Sacred Deer that thought provoking (though still fun).

But what is their order? Logically using “greater than” in between would suggest that Poor Things is their favorite. However, I’ve seen several posters using “>” as an arrow to suggest ascending order. Either way I’m going to disagree because either The Killing of a Sacred Deer is their least preferred Yorgos movie, or they use “>” incorrectly.
I don't hate it, it's still a 7/10 for me

Oh good call, I didn’t catch that! I mentally read it as being in descending order from best to worst but now I’m not sure that was the intent haha. Doesn’t ebb my excitement for Poor Things though haha
I didn’t want to assume how much you liked it. That’s why I used “least preferred”.  I strongly disagree with you, but I’m fine with you having different opinions.

I don't think it's a deciding factor to me. Poor Things is my new favourite of Lanthimos' after first watch, but I'll reserve full judgement until I've seen it again. If I was ranking them today, from most to least favourite (I like them all):

- Poor Things
- The Killing Of A Sacred Deer
- The Favourite
- Dogtooth
- The Lobster

I still haven't seen Alps but will be watching it soon.

I find him very frustrating to be honest, in principle I should love him but I just don’t. 

The Lobster was interesting and was a rather funny play on modern relationships and dating. But it spent too long drawing out punchline scenes and really dry dark humour that reminded me of some sort of Curb your enthusiasm level of cringe humour. Which i must admit I have never liked. 

The film can’t stick with one idea and really unpack it, instead we just jump between a lot of potential ideas and stories that don’t go anywhere. 

It is funny, but in a light chuckle way. Frankly have no desire to rewatch it. And the characters were too inhuman. The idea of presenting human traits through schizoid mumble core characters just wasn’t enough for me. 

It was missing a real home run of a punchline or story arc resolution. It’s meandering may be the point but that doesn’t make it better. 

Killing of a Sacred Deer feels so much like a weird mash up of the Shining that it just makes me want to go and watch that because it vastly superior to this. 

Again it has almost everything, looks beautiful, sounds amazing, great acting and an initial build up of tension. Then it is completely ruined in the scene where spaghetti kid literally spews out the entire plot in the space of a few minutes. I get that may have been intentionally crass or surreal but I hated the whole thing and the film quickly deteriorates afterwards. 

Again interesting ideas, poor execution. Much too intentionally absurd without earning it within the films universe. 

There are moments of brilliance, like the insanely unsettling scene where the girl sings to Spaghetti kid. 

But so much unearned or just jarring. I get they were trying yo show the manic swinging of emotions as the parents come to terms with what they have to do, but in the end its sloppy. 

Also that Bach piece at the end just made me cringe. At least he didn’t use Mozarts Requiem. 

The forced need to adhere to mumblecore throughout the film really shoots itself in the foot for most of his films. Even in KOASD they manage to have characters quietly get violently angry and lose their minds. It is so forced. 

For how much this film reveres and takes after The Shining it seems unaware of what made that film an all time classic, Jack Nicholson and his intentional emotive over acting. 

There is more genuine human emotion when Jack Torrence is yelling and flailing to himself after being acvused of hurting Danny, then the hallucinatory bar scene. Or the scene where he has the conversation with Danny just before he loses it. Or when he does lose it and the classic scene between him and Wendy. 

The Shining would be a shell of a film without this. And again the forced mumblecore style basically ruins any chance of evoking anything close to as hard hitting or potent. 

I feel so detached from his films that I never am able to connect or truly care what is going on. 

His aesthetic beauty and base creativity just isn’t enough for me. 

But I am aware I’m in the minority, I just think he rubs me the wrong way.

So I suppose you didn't like Dogtooth either. 

What about The Favourite and Poor Things?
Based on their response to me, your initial assumption is correct. Poor Things is their favorite.
I haven't seen Poor Things yet but I'm seeing some reviews from feminist critics thats its quite shallow and reductive.

I came here after wondering to myself: "why didn't I care as much for The Favourite and Poor Things as I did his previous work?" I think I've discovered that it's Lanthimos' writing that I'm attracted to as much as his direction!
